notes: The file viewer shows images, plays video and audio, and diffs changed images, instead of the binary stub. src/main/server/media.ts classifies a file by signature first (PNG, JPEG, GIF, RIFF/WEBP, RIFF/WAVE, ISO BMFF brands for mp4/mov/m4a/avif/heic, EBML for webm/mkv, Ogg, FLAC, ID3) and extension second, and the new `fs.media` route (contract-fsgit.ts, fsgit.ts) answers {kind, mime, url, size, mtimeMs} or null for anything that is not media or lies outside the open project and workspace roots (setMediaRoots in server/index.ts). The bytes never cross the WebSocket: the URL is `tempcode-asset://file/<token>/<name>?v=<mtime>`, a random per-path token the renderer cannot forge into a disk path, and the `file` host in src/main/assets.ts re-checks the real path against the real roots on every request (a symlink that leaves a root, or a root that closed, is refused) and streams from disk with Content-Type, Accept-Ranges, Content-Length, 206/Content-Range and 416, so a large video scrubs. `git.fileMedia` (gitops.ts) materialises the index or ref side of a changed media file under a scratch dir by blob hash for the review view. In the renderer, MediaGate (surfaces/MediaViewer.tsx) sits in FilePane in front of both editors: an image is centred on a flat neutral background, lazy and async decoded, with a Fit / 1:1 toggle in the existing footer strip beside its pixel size and byte size; video is a focused native <video controls> at its natural aspect, audio an <audio controls>; a review tab shows the git side beside the working file; a file Chromium cannot decode (HEIC) says so; everything else falls through to the editor and its binary stub. Tests: media.test.ts (sniffing, extension fallback, Range math, fence inside/outside/symlink, 200/206/416/403 responses), MediaViewer.dom.test.tsx (image/video/audio/stub/review). Verified over CDP in an isolated dev instance and in a packaged signed build: png, gif, svg, jpg, bmp, big png at 1:1, mp4 (H.264), mov, webm, mp3, m4a all render or play with readyState 4 and 206 Range responses; heic shows the decode notice; .ts opens the editor and a .bin keeps the stub.
